title: Microsoft 365 account takeover cleanup
product: Microsoft Entra ID and Exchange Online
use_case: When a Microsoft 365 account is taken over, reset the user's password to a random one, revoke their sign-in sessions, make them change their password at the next sign-in, turn off inbox rules that forward, redirect or delete mail, confirm them as compromised in Entra ID where the tenant has Entra ID P2, and record the inbox rules before and after on the case.
trigger: Platform Events, source Identity Findings, event Created, or source Alert2 (detections), event create, each with the Only When filter in SETUP.md. Or User Initiated, a Response Action on Case, to run it by hand from a case.
connections: Taegis.MicrosoftGraphAPI 2.12.2, the Microsoft Graph API connector Sophos manages, to look users up, reset and expire passwords, revoke sessions, turn off inbox rules and confirm compromise
Taegis.Case 1.0.5 and Taegis.Alert 1.3.6, the case and detection connectors Sophos manages, to read the case's detections and add the comment
requires: Microsoft 365 with Exchange Online mailboxes, a Microsoft Graph API connection with the permissions in SETUP.md, Microsoft Entra ID P2 for Confirm compromised (skipped without it), Sophos ITDR for the identity finding trigger, and Sophos Fusion playbooks under Security Operations > Automations
mdr_note: Sophos MDR doesn't run or watch this playbook, and Sophos MDR may already be acting on the same user. A run from a case acts only on self-managed cases unless you turn on Include Sophos-managed cases. The identity finding and detection triggers don't check who works the detection, so agree them with the Sophos MDR team first.
rollback: Turn the inbox rules back on (the case comment names them), enable the account if Disable account was on, and dismiss the user's risk in Entra ID. Revoked sessions stay revoked and the old password can't be restored, so the user signs in with a new one from your helpdesk or self-service password reset.
author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: This playbook cleans up a taken-over Microsoft 365 account: it resets the user's password to a random one, revokes their sessions, makes them change it at the next sign-in, turns off inbox rules that forward, redirect or delete mail, confirms them as compromised where the tenant has Entra ID P2, and comments the rules before and after. It runs on a Sophos ITDR leaked credential finding, a Microsoft detection or by hand from a case, through the Microsoft Graph API connector. Dry run is on.
notes:
Setup:
- Every step is one setting. Disable account is off unless you turn it on.
- Confirm compromised needs Microsoft Entra ID P2. Without it the playbook skips that step and says why.
- Reset the password sets a random one the connector makes for each call. Leave the connection's Password to use in response actions setting at its default: a fixed value gives every reset user the same password.
- There is no Active Directory step: Fusion wants a connection for every connector a template lists. The comment flags synced users.
- There's no approval step. Dry run, Domains, Excluded users and Max users per run are the controls.

How it works:
- It resets the password before revoking sessions, and keeps the reset's request out of the execution log, so the new password isn't recorded.
- A finding run acts on the finding's user. A detection run acts on the userName entities with an @, or targetUserName when there are none. A run by hand from a case acts on the users in all of the case's detections.
- It turns off an inbox rule only when the rule is on and forwards, forwards as an attachment, redirects, deletes or permanently deletes mail. Rules that only move or mark mail are listed and left on.
- With dry run off it reads the inbox rules again afterwards, so the comment shows the result, not the request.
- A detection run waits up to Seconds to wait for the case, then comments on it. A finding run has no case, so its outcome is only in the execution.

Testing:
- On 2026-11-15 the dsl passed playbookValidateDSLV2 with no errors or warnings in two Sophos Fusion test tenants, us01 and eu02.
- In the us01 tenant a renamed copy ran by hand 15 times against a test user in a test Microsoft 365 tenant, through the Marketplace Microsoft Graph API connection, with made-up detections and ITDR finding and a real test case. It revoked sessions, required a password change, disabled the account and turned off three test rules that forwarded, redirected and deleted mail, leaving a mark-as-read rule and one already off alone. Entra ID, the mailbox and the audit log were read back.
- It also handled dry run, a repeat run, Max users per run, Excluded users, other domains, titles and categories, an unknown user and a case with no detections.
- 6 more runs on 2026-11-15 used a new test user. On Entra ID P1, 1.0.0 ended FAIL on the not licensed reply; 1.1.0 skipped Confirm compromised and ended SUCCESS in all 5 of its runs. After the reset the old password was refused, the audit log showed Reset user password, and the execution log held no password.

Known gaps:
- Confirm compromised wasn't tested with Entra ID P2; the test tenant has P1.
- No real ITDR finding or Microsoft detection was used; both were made up in the shapes Fusion reads. The case menu run wasn't tested: the API refuses User Initiated runs.
- MFA methods, OAuth app consents and mailbox forwarding set in Exchange Online aren't covered. A synced user wasn't tested; resetting one needs password writeback.
